principle: Every source field maps to a base type of a closed, versioned vocabulary through a closed, versioned reader. Structured data are combinations of base types (or of other published structured types). Structured types are NOT a closed list: the agent proposes them through MCP, the human approves them in the THS, the Semantic Registry publishes them as DATATYPE artifacts, and Ingestion and UDP accept any published structured type by contract, without type-specific code.
emptyValue: For every reader except IDENTITY, a cell that is empty or only whitespace is ABSENT: no value is produced (the property or component is omitted) and no error is raised. IDENTITY keeps the lexical cell unchanged, including empty strings, for compatibility with data already acquired. Required checks belong to the structured type component or to the mapping, not to readers.
invalidValue: A value that a reader, constructor or structured type cannot accept is a DATA error with a stable code; the error never contains the source value (D-058).
provenance: When the canonical value differs from the source lexical value(s), the source lexical value(s) are preserved in provenance/evidence (PET Ingestion 10.2).

baseTypes.canonical: JSON string, as produced by the reader

JSON string of plain integer digits with optional leading '-', no , no leading zeros, no exponent (e.g. "-42"); a string, not a JSON number, so that generic JSON consumers never convert it to binary floating point; consumers parse with BigInteger/BigDecimal

JSON string of the plain decimal value with '.' as separator, no exponent, trailing zeros stripped (BigDecimal.stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString(), e.g. "45.6495"); a string, not a JSON number, so that generic JSON consumers never convert it to binary floating point; consumers parse with BigDecimal
JSON string ISO-8601 instant normalized to UTC with 'Z' (e.g. 2026-11-22T09:15:00Z); the source offset or zone is kept in provenance
JSON object {"crs": "EPSG:<n>", "geoJson": <RFC 7946 geometry>} as already stored by UDP; coordinates [x, y] = [lon, lat] for EPSG:4326
JSON string, absolute IRI of a concept of a published controlled vocabulary

readers.rule: Unicode NFC, then trim leading/trailing whitespace
after trim and lower-case (Locale.ROOT): true = {sì, si, s, vero, v, true, 1}; false = {no, n, falso, f, false, 0}; anything else is invalid
ISO-8601 date-time with explicit offset (Z or +hh:mm); seconds optional; fraction up to 9 digits
YYYY-MM-DD[T| ]HH:mm[:ss] without offset, interpreted in Europe/Rome; a local time in a DST gap or overlap is invalid (no guessing)
RFC 7946 geometry object text; CRS EPSG:4326
OGC WKT geometry text with the CRS declared in params
exact match of the trimmed code in the published value map referenced by valueMapRef; unmapped code is invalid

constructors.rule: Point [lon, lat] in EPSG:4326; lat in [-90, 90], lon in [-180, 180]; both inputs absent -> ABSENT; exactly one absent -> invalid
join the non-absent parts in declared order with the separator; all parts absent -> ABSENT

params.itemReaderParams: optional object, the params of itemReader (crs for WKT_V1, valueMapRef for VALUE_MAP_V1), same keys as transformParams

constructors.rule: split on the separator, apply itemReader to each item, skip absent items; the result is a JSON array of the itemReader output type; no items -> ABSENT

structuredTypes.owner: Semantic Registry, new artifact type DATATYPE (native proposal through MCP semantic.propose, THS approval, publication in a publication set; immutable once published, a change is a new semanticVersion).
structuredTypes.datatypeIri: The DATATYPE semanticId is the datatype IRI of values of that type. Mappings pin it as <semanticId>@<publicationSetId> like every other semantic reference.

definition.components: 1 to 32 items {name, type, cardinality, required, labels?}
definition.name: ^[a-z][A-Za-z0-9]{0,63}$, unique within the type
definition.type: a base type id, or the IRI of another PUBLISHED DATATYPE pinned as <semanticId>@<publicationSetId>
definition.constraints: optional, closed set per component: {minInclusive, maxInclusive} for integer/decimal/date/datetime as JSON strings in the canonical form of the component type (e.g. "-90", "45.5", "2026-01-01", "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"); {maxLength} for string as a JSON integer; {vocabularyRef} for concept as the absolute IRI of a published vocabulary

structuredTypes.limits: nesting depth at most 4; at most 32 components per type and 256 leaf components in total; no cycles (a type cannot contain itself directly or indirectly)
structuredTypes.canonical: JSON object with exactly the defined component names present for non-absent values; ONE -> canonical value of the component type; MANY -> JSON array of canonical values (no empty arrays: an empty MANY component is ABSENT). Unknown keys are invalid. A required component absent -> invalid. All components absent -> the structured value is ABSENT.
structuredTypes.identity: JSON_V1 on the canonical JSON (keys sorted), unless the mapping declares a component-level signal
structuredTypes.pinning: Onboarding embeds in the published bundle the exact definition of every pinned DATATYPE (and of the DATATYPEs it contains) with its SHA-256; Ingestion and UDP verify definition and hash against the Semantic Registry (references:resolve) like every other semantic reference, then apply the definition generically. New preparations (Onboarding review prepare) require every pinned DATATYPE, nested ones included, to be ACTIVE; consumers resolving an already published bundle (historical replay) accept ACTIVE, DEPRECATED or RETIRED pins, like every other semantic reference.
structuredTypes.conceptMembership: A concept value is a member of the component vocabularyRef when either (a) the concept is a pinned CONCEPT of that vocabulary in the bundle, or (b) it was produced by VALUE_MAP_V1 with a value map pinned in the bundle (valueMapRef@publicationSetId) whose published target vocabulary equals vocabularyRef. Onboarding embeds the value map pin and its target vocabulary in the bundle; UDP and Ingestion accept membership only through (a) or (b).

mappingShape.field: Each source field keeps {fieldName, extractionDecision, dataAccessLabel, targetPropertyIri?, transform?} as today; 'transform' is a reader id (default IDENTITY) and the new optional 'transformParams' object carries the reader params (crs, valueMapRef, separator, itemReader). The existing 'valueMapRef' field stays accepted as an alias of transformParams.valueMapRef.
mappingShape.composition: New optional top-level array 'compositions'. Each item is either {kind: 'CONSTRUCTOR', constructorId, targetPropertyIri, dataAccessLabel, inputs: [{role, fieldName, reader, transformParams?}], params} or {kind: 'STRUCTURED', typeRef: '<DATATYPE semanticId>@<publicationSetId>', targetPropertyIri, dataAccessLabel, components: [{component, fieldName, reader, transformParams?} | {component, constructor: {constructorId, inputs, params}} | {component, structured: {typeRef, components}}]}. Every reference resolves to an INCLUDE field of the same file; reader/constructor output types must equal the component or input type. For a component with cardinality MANY, the builder is {component, items: [<builder>, ...]} where each item is one of the single builders above (field+reader, constructor, structured); absent items are skipped; no non-absent item -> the component is ABSENT. A MANY component may also be built by LIST_SPLIT_V1 from one field.
mappingShape.fieldUse: A field referenced only by compositions may be INCLUDE without targetPropertyIri. A field may also map to its own property and feed a composition.
